title: Make Zedu marketing email preferences clear and testable
description: Design the subscription experience for optional Zedu marketing messages, separate from essential account and service notices. Inventory proposed message categories; draft opt-in, confirmation, frequency choices, unsubscribe and preference-update copy; define suppression and re-subscription rules. Deliver a state diagram and test cases for unsubscribe, duplicate signup and conflicting preferences, with privacy-review questions. Done when the team approves the flow and every marketing category has an explicit preference and accountable owner. Reuse existing welcome/newsletter content and sender-authentication work; do not rewrite campaigns, send emails or change live mailing lists. Legal and implementation approval remain dependencies.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Classify every message as service or marketing first, so essential notices never sit behind an unsubscribe
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Unsubscribe rules only work if the line between service messages (security alerts, invites, billing) and marketing is drawn first. Approach: list every email Zedu sends or plans to send, classify each as service or marketing using the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 and common email practice, and mark borderline cases (product tips, feature announcements) for a team decision. Done: the classified inventory, the rule for borderline cases, and the check that no service message carries a marketing unsubscribe link and no marketing message is sent without consent.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Start from the one sign-up that exists today, then add categories, consent wording and an unsubscribe path around it
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Today the only marketing opt-in is the footer form: it posts just an email to /newsletter (production code Cybertron-HNG/zedu-fe, footer/index.tsx line 152), with no category choice, no consent wording and a confirmation that reads 'Email sent successfully!'. Plan: 1) inventory the message categories the team proposes (newsletter, product updates, events, onboarding tips) and separate them from essential account and service email; 2) write the opt-in wording, confirmation, frequency choices, preference page, unsubscribe and re-subscribe copy, and define suppression rules, with a state diagram; 3) write test cases for unsubscribe, duplicate sign-up and conflicting preferences, plus the privacy-review questions, aligned with the open goal that brings the privacy policy up to the NDPA 2023. Tasks: category inventory and state diagram (research), copy and test cases (content).

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Test preference controls for accessibility and recovery
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Add a focused accessibility and recovery pass to the marketing email preference flow. Define keyboard, screen-reader and mobile checks for opt-in, category changes, unsubscribe, errors, confirmation and resubscribe. Deliver test cases with expected outcomes and an issue log; use only screens that can be verified and label unavailable states as untested. This fills an accessibility and failure-recovery gap beyond the accepted copy and state diagram. No emails are sent and no live mailing lists are changed.
